synopsis: ISO 19014-2 covers safety-control systems that control machine motion or mitigate hazards, but excludes awareness-only systems; adding a brake command therefore moves collision mitigation into its scope [f2311, f2075, f15175]. The booklet treats automatic braking as a new safety-control function rather than a warning function with a brake added, requiring validation of brake-command integrity, faults, degraded modes, unintended activation and failure to activate—not just perception statistics [f10476, f5223, f5810]. Part 2 addresses hardware, architecture and achieved Machine Performance Level (MPLa), including architecture evaluation, component reliability, fault behaviour and diagnostics; safety-function performance under expected environmental conditions must also be demonstrated and documented [f2318, f2693, f7735]. As of 1 October 2026, the published edition was still 2022, while Edition 2 had been at stage 60.00, “under publication,” since 22 August 2026 and was scheduled for October; Chapter 12 instead describes the revision as being at FDIS, creating a status discrepancy [f2319, f2320, f9771]. The forthcoming editions’ final texts were unavailable for review, so their final content remained uncertain and publication status should be rechecked before design freeze [f2862, f6286].
